MAJOR — The 4px density migration lands FIRST, not last, contradicting the stated ordering constraint. Contracts Task 4 does not merely declare the tokens: Steps 2–4 run the `perl` sweep over app.css, delete `--sp-*`, and add `line-height` to `body` — the 92-declaration change spec §4.F.6 calls "a visible density change; every screen is reviewed afterwards". So the density change is in the tree before a single A/B/C/D/E task runs, and F Task 122's review of it happens roughly 120 tasks later. Two concrete consequences the parts have already noticed but not resolved: (a) A Task 81's expected `{"left":6,"right":1}` and Task 82's `{"tabTop":4,"tabBottom":43}` are stated as absolutes without saying which side of Task 4 they were measured on, while F Task 115 explicitly records that its own numbers moved from `[-24,-4]` to `[-26,-5]` because of it; (b) F's own preamble states the 26 inline `var(--sp-*)` uses in eight `.tsx` files "will resolve to nothing … until Task 116 runs", so the Open/Scratch row, the profile chip rows and five settings sections render with gaps collapsed to 0 for the entire duration of A, B, C, D and E — and `npm run check`, which D Task 40 Step 6 and A Task 94 Step 6 both assert exits 0, cannot see it. Fix: split contracts Task 4 into 4a (declare `--space-*`, `--lh-*`, `--icon-*`, `--tab-indicator`, `--tab-dot-worklog`, `--ring-full`, `--traffic-lights-w`, `--scrim`, `--swatch-ring`, `--shadow-panel`, `--on-danger` ALONGSIDE the existing `--sp-*` block, changing no rule and moving no pixel) and 4b (the perl sweep, the `--sp-*` deletion, `body` line-height, the remote/style.css literal). Move 4b to the head of workstream F, immediately before Task 116, and merge the two into one commit so the whole density change is contiguous and F Task 122 reviews it while it is fresh.

MAJOR — A Task 90 is too large to be one reviewable unit and several of its steps are not single actions. Step 4 alone edits `startSession`'s options type and tab literal, rewrites its `setTabs`, adds `activeNewTabId`, threads `replaceTabId` through four launcher call sites plus two inside the `<Launcher>` element, updates four dependency arrays, and repeats the whole shape for `startHostSession`. Step 5 edits three more regions. Step 6 replaces two large JSX blocks. That is nine App.tsx regions in one task and well over an hour with no intermediate verification. Split into: 90a seed a New tab at boot and stop `activeTabId` ever being null (Steps 2–3 + Step 5's guards); 90b `replaceTabId` on `startSession`/`startHostSession`; 90c render the launcher as the active New tab's content (Step 6). Each ends in a build and one measurement.

MAJOR — C Task 26 Step 1 replaces the whole ~75-line `runWorklogScan` in a single step, and in doing so lands five separable changes at once: the `lastScanReport`/`reportScan` machinery, the never-throws contract, the remote-cwd rule, the `boards` threading, and the budget-vs-nothing branch. Its diff cannot be reviewed against any one claim. Same class of problem in C Task 22 (six source edits across seven runner.ts functions), C Task 31 Steps 3–6 (AutoScanner options + constructor + `observe` + `snapshot()` + `save()` + two call sites, plus a new module), D Task 40 (a 220-line suite in Step 1 and a 175-line module in Step 3), E Task 8 Step 5 (the whole 110-line `UsageChip`), and F Task 117 Step 4 (a fifteen-row call-site table across six files plus three `data-size` additions). None of these is a 2–5 minute action. At minimum, split C 26 and C 31; the others should be re-cut into one file or one function per step.

MAJOR — F Task 122 Step 4 is not a step. "Fix what the images show, one commit per fix" is unbounded work with no exit condition, no list of what counts as a defect, and no acceptance criterion. It is the task the spec explicitly asks for (§4.F.6, "every screen is reviewed afterwards"), so it must not be dropped — but it needs a bounded form: enumerate the four named failure modes from Step 3 as four explicit checks with pass/fail wording, and make anything beyond them a follow-up issue rather than an open-ended edit inside this task.

Contracts Task 2 Step 7 adds `kind: 'session'`, `hostId`, `selectedPath`, `expandedPath` to the Tab literals in App.tsx (including `hostId: host.id` at line 427); A Task 90 Step 4 then instructs "add `kind: 'session' as const, hostId: null, selectedPath: null, expandedPath: null` to the `tab` literal" and "`hostId: host.id`" again. Neither is harmful, but each will stall an executor who finds the change already present. Mark both as "already landed — verify, do not re-add".

MODERATE — Twelve tasks across five parts insert into the same four verify suites using the anchor "immediately before the final `console.log` / the file's last two lines". `scripts/verify-profiles.mts` receives insertions from B 61, B 62 (no — that is verify-settings), B 63, B 64, B 66 and D 45; `verify-worklog-gate.mts` from contracts Task 1, C 27, C 29 and C 30; `verify-worklog-runner.mts` from C 21, C 22, C 24 and C 25; `verify-folders.mts` from D 40, 41, 46 and 47; `verify-context.mts` from A 86 and E 6 (twice, at two different anchors). The relative anchor is sound and will keep working, but every quoted "currently line N" alongside it will be stale by the time the later ones run. MINOR — A Task 83 ships a `TabIndicator` branch (`kind === 'new'`, the ring-plus glyph, the `New session, not started` label) that is dead code and untested for ten tasks, because no `new` tab exists until A Task 90 Step 7. Harmless, but note it in Task 83 so its Step 7 measurement is not expected to exercise that branch.

MINOR — Ordering within workstream E is sound and self-consistent (parse → generate → settings file → argv → install → meter → renderer → chip → setting → docs), and it is correctly the workstream everything numeric depends on. But nothing in the plan states the cross-workstream sequence anywhere in one place. Add an explicit global order to the contracts section: contracts 1–4a → E (renumbered) → C → A → B → D → F (4b + 110–122), with the three cross-edges called out — E before A Task 94's context-ring measurements, C Task 28 before A Task 85, F Task 115/117 before D Task 43/44.
verdict: Spec coverage is close to complete: every numbered item in §4.A (9/9), §4.B (6/6, one delivered by relabelling rather than recolouring), §4.D (5/5) and §4.E (5/5) has a task, as do §4.C 1–5, 7, 8 and §4.F 1–10. Three items have no task at all — §4.C.6's "editable IDs" (storage is done, no UI exists anywhere), §5's "verify:usage — repoint at the statusLine payload" (that suite is never touched), and §6's "set the worklog target to Notion only" (asserted by D Task 47, never written by anything). Ordering is where this plan is not yet executable. Five blockers: contracts Task 5 and E Tasks 1–3 are the same work and each expects the other not to have run; E's task numbers collide with the contracts' 1–5; F Task 111 and A Tasks 90–92 implement §4.F.1 twice against mutually deleted state; D Task 44 rewrites the exact JSX F 115/117 just cleaned up and puts every inline size back; and A Task 85's acceptance test needs C Task 28's handlers that no prerequisite names. Beyond those, the stated constraint that F's 4px migration lands last is violated by contracts Task 4, which performs the whole 92-declaration density change before any workstream runs and leaves 26 inline token uses rendering at 0 through all of A–E — split it into declare-then-migrate and move the migration to the head of F. Four tasks (A 90, C 26, C 31, F 117 Step 4) are too large to review as one unit, and F Task 122 Step 4 is unbounded. Fix the five blockers, the Task 4 split, and the six unfilled measurement placeholders in C Tasks 24–25 before execution; the rest can be corrected in place.

verdict: Not ready to execute as-is. The type surface is largely coherent — every IPC channel, settings key and shared type used in A–F traces back to a contracts definition, and the ones that don't (`GroupOwner`, `windowFor`, `userStatusLineCommand`, `src/shared/statusLine.ts`, `--surface-selected`, `--chevron`, `--control-h`, `WorklogBudgetError`, `isBudgetExhausted`, `watchStateFrom`, `autoScanStateFile`) are self-consistent additions their own parts declare. But there are eight hard collisions where two parts write incompatible code into the same lines: `scripts/cdp-eval.mjs` (four rival implementations), `selectProject` in App.tsx (A vs F, with A renaming the state F writes), the `offWatch` subscription in App.tsx's bootstrap effect (A vs C — a literal duplicate `const` in one block), the `.project-top` JSX in Sidebar.tsx (D re-adds exactly the inline styles and icon attributes F deletes), `openFolder`'s `setActiveTabId(null)` (A asserts zero occurrences, F says keep it), `--on-danger` (contracts `#ffffff` vs F `var(--bg)`, and F is right), the `check` script in package.json (E pastes a full line that drops three suites), and contracts Task 5 vs E Tasks 1-3 (the same two files created twice). Two ordering assumptions are unsatisfiable as written: contracts Task 1 Step 6 cannot pass until B Task 60's tsconfig change lands, and A Task 85's measurement needs C Task 28's IPC handler. One shipped-value placeholder is dangerous rather than merely unfinished: `RECALL_MAX_BUDGET_USD = 0` (and `APPLY_MAX_BUDGET_USD` inheriting it) passes its own guard assertions vacuously, so `npm run check` goes green on a $0 budget ceiling — worse than the $0.15 the workstream exists to raise. Fix the eight collisions, hoist cdp-eval.mjs and the tsconfig flag into the contracts section, resolve the statusLine duplication, and add a non-vacuous assertion on the budget constants; after that the plan is executable.

specGaps.specItem: CLAUDE.md convention: "Relative imports in src/main carry explicit .ts extensions" — extended by contract §0.7 to "shared modules use extensionless relative imports"
specGaps.why: Contract Task 1 Step 5 writes `export { foldGroup } from './paths'` into src/shared/profiles.ts. Also correct §0.7's blanket "extensionless" wording to "extensionless for type-only; explicit .ts for values".

specGaps.specItem: CLAUDE.md gotcha 6: "The docked browser is its own CDP target. Test scripts that attach by type === 'page' must filter on the URL or they drive the wrong page."
specGaps.why: Three of the four cdp-eval.mjs implementations claim to honour this and do not. D Task 42's filter is `t.type === 'page' && (t.url.startsWith('file://') || /^https?:\/\/localhost:\d+\//.test(t.url))`; E Task 7's is `t.url.includes('/index.html') || /localhost:\d+\/?$/`; F Task 110's is `t.url.includes('/out/renderer/index.html') || t.url.includes('localhost:5173')`. Stoke's docked browser exists precisely so the user can point it at a local dev server, so `localhost:<port>` and `file://` are exactly the URLs it will be showing — and `Array.find` returns whichever target the browser enumerates first. Only A Task 80's version is safe: it confirms `typeof window.stoke === 'object' && typeof window.stoke.platform === 'string'`, which no docked-browser page can have (contextBridge is only injected into the renderer). Fix: use A's identification in the single surviving copy. Note A's own header comment is wrong — it says "Targets are NOT filtered by type === 'page'" while the code does `targets.filter((t) => t.type === 'page' && t.webSocketDebuggerUrl)`; reword it to "filtered to page targets, then identified by window.stoke".

specGaps.specItem: CLAUDE.md verification expectations: "`npm run check` must pass."
specGaps.why: D Task 47 Step 4 adds a block to scripts/verify-folders.mts — which D Task 40 Step 5 chains into `check` — that reads the user's live settings file at ~/Library/Application Support/stoke/settings.json and asserts `real.projectRoots` equals exactly `['/Users/thevinh/dev/work']` and `real.worklogBoards.targets` equals exactly `['notion']`. `npm run check` then fails the first time the user adds a second scan root or ticks ClickUp — a false failure in the one command CLAUDE.md says must always pass, and it fails in a suite whose name suggests nothing about settings. verify:context also reads the real machine, but it asserts invariants about transcripts rather than the exact value of a user-editable setting. Fix: keep the "every folder under the work root is watched" assertion (that is a real invariant) and drop the two exact-value checks, or move the whole block behind a `measure:`-style script excluded from `check`, like measure:worklog and verify:usage already are.

specGaps.specItem: CLAUDE.md gotcha 20: "an await inside a polling pass is a window two passes can both walk through… Setting the claim after the await is not enough."
specGaps.why: Not reintroduced — C Task 31 gets this right, and deliberately. Its `this.save()` calls are placed after `session.scanning = false` in the `!watched` branch of `evaluate()` and inside `run()`'s `finally`, both synchronous, both inside the existing `evaluating` guard and after the existing claim-before-await at autoscan.ts:260. `StoredActivity` also excludes `scanning` on purpose, so a crashed process cannot come back with a session permanently claimed. One residual gap worth a line: `run()` pushes `started` onto `recentScans` before awaiting the scan but nothing persists until the run returns, so a crash mid-scan loses that hour's spend from the ceiling. Either call `this.save()` after the `recentScans.push(started)` or state in StoredActivity's comment that the ceiling is best-effort across a crash.

specGaps.specItem: CLAUDE.md gotcha 19: "Do not add flags to a user's remote connect command."
specGaps.why: Honoured, and worth recording so nobody 'improves' it later. E Task 5 Step 1 writes `const settingsFile = opts.host ? null : sessionSettings(sessionId)` and keeps `opts.host ? buildSshArgs(opts.host) : buildArgs({ ...opts, sessionId }, settingsFile)`, so an SSH session gets no `--settings` and therefore no statusLine payload. The consequence is unstated in the plan and should be: SSH sessions keep the old banner/observed-usage context inference and contribute nothing to the usage chip. Add that sentence to E Task 5's commit body and to the CLAUDE.md gotcha 2 rewrite in E Task 10 Step 1, which currently only carves out `--continue`.

specGaps.specItem: CLAUDE.md gotcha 13: execFile maxBuffer / cmd.exe metacharacter eating
specGaps.why: Honoured. E's `statusLineCommand` travels inside a `--settings` file, never on an argv, and E Task 2 Step 1 asserts `/[&|<>^]/.test(cmd) === false` plus `/^"[^"]+" "<id>"$/`. One residual: the shim path is `join(tmpdir(), 'stoke', 'statusline', 'run.cmd')`, and on Windows a username containing `&` or `^` would put a metacharacter inside the quoted path. The existing assertion catches it because it runs against the real `statusLineDir()`, so no change is needed — but the wrapper's own re-exec (`execFileSync(shell, [win ? '/c' : '-c', cmd], …)` where `cmd` is the user's own statusLine command read off disk) is the one place a user string does reach a shell. That is intentional (it is their command, run as they configured it) and should be said so in the comment, because it otherwise reads as the exact mistake gotcha 13 warns about.

verdict: The plan is unusually disciplined about the twenty gotchas — I found no parameter properties, no hardcoded colours in components, no channel invented outside src/shared/ipc.ts, no fourth row on the `.app` grid, no renderer-DOM overlay over a WebContentsView, no terminal assertion from textContent, no change to the worklog create dedupe key, and no flag added to the SSH connect command (E Task 5 explicitly passes `null` for the settings file when `opts.host` is set). Gotcha 20 is handled correctly and knowingly by C Task 31. But it is not ready to execute as ordered. Three defects will stop a run dead: contract Task 1 breaks `verify:profiles` and its own Step 6 asserts the opposite (the fix, B Task 60, is scheduled too late); C Tasks 29 and 30 append `ok(...)` assertions to a suite that only defines `check()`, taking `npm run check` down; and C Task 21's gotcha-17 regression test — the single guard protecting every rejected proposal from resurrection — calls `dedupeKey` without importing it from queue.ts, so it never runs. Two more are silent rather than loud: three of the four rival `scripts/verify-cdp-eval` implementations select their CDP target by URL patterns the docked browser legitimately matches (gotcha 6, the exact failure), and D Task 47 wires one machine's live settings values into `npm run check`. Add the four unmeasured budget placeholders in C Tasks 24–25 (a shipped `RECALL_MAX_BUDGET_USD = 0` reproduces spec 2.4.1 exactly) and the cdp-eval / Icons-props / package.json-check-line collisions, and this needs one reconciliation pass before Task 1.
